title: Coulomb- and exchange-driven redistribution of spectral correlations
authors: Zanya Gonzalez Tellez, Miguel Angel Ocaña Bribiesca
abstract: Electronic correlations reorganize not only the energies of individual electronic states but also the collective structure of the spectrum. Here, first-principles density functional theory calculations combined with random-matrix spectral statistics are used to examine this reorganization in gamma-Ce within a static spin-polarized DFT+U+SOC description. We distinguish the effects of the Coulomb interaction U from those of the exchange interaction J by analyzing nearest-neighbor spacings, reduced spacing ratios, band velocities, and band curvatures across the Ce-4f manifold. Increasing U does not produce a monotonic transition between Poisson- and Wigner-Dyson-like statistics; instead, the region of strongest level repulsion migrates across the 4f manifold as the interaction increases. Exchange produces a qualitatively different response. At fixed U, strongly repulsive and strongly clustered spectral regions coexist within the same 4f manifold even while the total spin moment and 4f occupation remain nearly unchanged. The clustering persists after resolving the spectrum into its dominant j = 5/2 and j = 7/2 components and differs strongly between calculations having the same numerical value of U-J. Within the present DFT+U+SOC description, the spectral response therefore depends on the separate Coulomb and exchange interactions and cannot be represented completely by a single effective U-J parameter. These results show that energy- and character-resolved spectral statistics expose correlation-driven electronic reorganization that is hidden by conventional integrated observables.
summary: This theoretical study uses advanced spectral statistics on DFT+U+SOC calculations for $\gamma$-Ce to disentangle the effects of Coulomb (U) and exchange (J) interactions on the electronic spectrum. It finds that the spectral reorganization is highly sensitive to whether U or J is varied independently, demonstrating that the two interactions contribute distinct, non-additive effects on the $4f$ manifold's spectral correlations.
main_problem: To investigate how the Coulomb (U) and exchange (J) components of local electronic interactions separately reorganize the collective structure of the electronic spectrum in $\gamma$-Ce.
main_result: The spectral response depends on the separate Coulomb and exchange interactions, as the exchange interaction causes a distinct clustering effect not captured by a single effective U-J parameter.
method: First-principles DFT+U+SOC calculations are combined with Random Matrix Theory (RMT) spectral statistics applied to energy- and character-resolved spectral windows.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Ce-4f manifold in $\gamma$-Ce, modeled using the DFT+U+SOC formalism to treat local electronic correlations.
key_observables: Nearest-neighbor spacings, reduced spacing ratios, band velocities, band curvatures, and spectral statistics ($\langle r angle$, $ eta_B$).
important_parameters: The interaction parameters U and J are varied independently, and the analysis is performed on energy-resolved subwindows and $j=5/2$ and $j=7/2$ components.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a static spin-polarized DFT+U+SOC description, and RMT ensembles are used only as statistical references.
figures_summary: Figures compare spectral statistics (velocity/curvature distributions) across different energy windows and relativistic character ($j=5/2$ vs $j=7/2$), showing distinct behaviors for U-driven migration and J-driven coexistence.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes spectral statistics by varying U (fixing J) and varying J (fixing U), comparing the results to show that the separate roles of U and J are crucial and cannot be reduced to a single effective interaction.
why_interesting: The detailed spectral analysis provides a highly sensitive probe into the nature of electronic correlations, revealing internal structure (like exchange-driven clustering) that is masked by standard, integrated observables.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Evolution of the electronic structure along the U cut (J = 0.0 eV). The upper panels display the total j-projected Ce-4f partial densities of states (pDOS) for (a) U = 0.0, (b) 4.08, and (c) 9.52 eV, with blue and orange lines representing the j = 5/2 and j = 7/2 components, respectively. The lower panels show the corresponding electronic band structures along the W →L path, where colored segments highlight states matching the dominant relativistic character. The shaded region marks the DOS-selected upper Ce-4f manifold used in the spectral statistical analysis.

Figure 2: Evolution of the electronic structure along the J cut at fixed U = 6.12 eV. The upper panels show the total j-projected Ce-4f partial densities of states (pDOS) for (a) J = 0.0, (b) 0.68, and (c) 0.95 eV, with blue and orange lines denoting the j = 5/2 and j = 7/2 components, respectively. The lower panels show the corresponding electronic band structures along the W →L path, with colored segments identifying states matching the dominant relativistic character. The shaded region marks the DOS-selected high-energy Ce-4f manifold used in the spectral statistical analysis.

Figure 3: Energy-resolved evolution of the mean reduced spacing ratio ⟨r⟩as a function of (a) Hubbard U (at J = 0.0 eV) and (b) exchange parameter J (at fixed U = 6.12 eV) for the different DOS-selected Ce-4f subwindows. Horizontal dashed lines represent the analytical Poisson, GOE, and GUE random matrix reference values.

Figure 4: Representative nearest-neighbor spacing distributions P(s) (upper panels) and reduced spacing-ratio distributions P(r) (lower panels) for selected spectral regions of the Ce-4f manifold. The columns correspond to the central window at U = 4.08 eV (J = 0.0 eV), and the central and upper windows at U = 6.12 eV and J = 0.68 eV, respectively. Analytical RMT reference distributions (Poisson, GOE, and GUE) are shown alongside the corresponding Brody fits and mean reduced spacing ratios ⟨r⟩.

Figure 5: Comparison of the band dynamics in the central (left panels) and upper (right panels) regions of the Ce-4f manifold at U = 6.12 eV and J = 0.68 eV. The signed scaled-velocity distributions P(˜v) (upper panels) characterize the local band slopes, while the normalized curvature- magnitude distributions P(˜c) (lower panels) display the typical curvature scale and the high-curvature tails.
